text:
Nick Seeler has been a Flyer for 360 games, a fifth-round pick from Eden Prairie who made himself a regular through blocked shots and hard minutes. This week Broad Street Hockey argued the Flyers may need to trade him sooner rather than later, and Sunday in Calgary brought the other kind of attention: Charlie O'Connor noted it was Seeler's failed clear that led to Joel Farabee's tying shorthanded goal, before Seeler made a big play of his own later.

He has five assists in 19 games, which is about his normal level of offense. The Flyers are close to even with him on the ice versus off it, at 42% of the expected goals, and they've been fortunate on goals in his minutes. His ice time has dipped by nearly two minutes a night lately.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with clean breakouts, 62% of exits with possession, and Evolving-Hockey had him better than his goals last season. Our range says 11 to 23 points over a full season. On a team going nowhere this spring, a steady veteran defenseman is exactly the sort of piece contenders call about.
headline: Seeler, a trade chip in Philadelphia
